metadata.title: PISA 2012 Results: Ready to Learn (Volume III) (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2012 volume reports results based on the PISA target population of 15-year-olds across 65 participating countries and economies, using PISA’s standard complex survey design. The report indicates that school principal questionnaire responses are weighted to be proportionate to the number of 15-year-olds enrolled in each school, implying the use of sampling/selection weights for school-level reporting. For student-level indicators, the publication discusses international averages and statistical significance, consistent with survey-weighted estimation under PISA’s sampling and quality assurance procedures, but it does not provide the specific student weight variable names in the excerpt provided. Because this is an OECD results volume (not an ML modeling paper), the appropriate weights are those defined in the PISA 2012 technical documentation; analysts should apply the official PISA sampling weights when reproducing estimates and should not treat the reported figures as unweighted descriptive counts.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This volume primarily reports descriptive and association results for engagement, drive, self-beliefs, and their relationships with mathematics performance, rather than providing an explicit ML pipeline with documented plausible-value (PV) handling or a specific missing-data imputation strategy in the provided text. While PISA uses PVs for cognitive achievement scales in general, this excerpt does not specify whether PVs were used for the mathematics performance outcomes in the reported associations, nor does it document a PV-combining rule. The report does, however, define missing-data symbols (e.g., categories not applying, too few observations, data not available/withdrawn), which indicates that missingness is handled through reporting conventions and data availability rules rather than a fully specified imputation method in the excerpt.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The PISA 2012 target population is defined as students aged 15 years 3 months to 16 years 2 months who are enrolled in school and have completed at least 6 years of formal schooling, regardless of institution type, full-time/part-time status, or public/private/foreign schooling. The report states that exclusions are governed by strict technical standards, with an overall exclusion rate within a country required to be below 5% to limit distortion of national mean scores; exclusions can occur at the school level (e.g., remote/inaccessible, very small schools, operational factors) or at the student level (e.g., intellectual disability or limited proficiency in the assessment language). The excerpt does not provide additional analytic-subsample filters specific to this volume’s engagement/drive/self-beliefs analyses, so the analytic sample is treated as the available PISA 2012 student sample for the specified countries/economies, subject to PISA’s standard exclusions and the availability of questionnaire responses for the relevant indicators.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2012 Results volume (Volume III: Ready to Learn) synthesizes students’ engagement with and at school, drive and motivation, and mathematics self-beliefs, and reports how these dispositions relate to mathematics performance. PISA 2012 assessed around 510,000 15-year-olds across 65 countries and economies using paper-based tests (about two hours per student) with optional computer-based components in some countries, plus student and school questionnaires (and optional parent questionnaires in selected systems). The report emphasizes that PISA cannot identify cause-and-effect relationships, but it can show how student and school characteristics are associated with outcomes and how these relationships vary by gender and socio-economic status. Missing data are handled through reporting conventions (e.g., categories not applying, too few observations, data not available/withdrawn), and international averages are computed as arithmetic means across country estimates. The excerpt does not specify PV-combining rules or missing-data imputation methods for the mathematics performance outcomes in the reported associations.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is an OECD results volume rather than an empirical ML study: it does not train or evaluate machine-learning models, and it does not provide a model-based predictive pipeline with PV/missing-data handling details in the provided text. Consequently, fields related to ML techniques and structured predictive findings are intentionally empty. The extraction is sparse for sample-size-by-country and for PV/missing-data mechanics because the excerpt focuses on conceptual framing, table/figure navigation, and high-level executive summary rather than the full technical annexes.
